_meta.directives: Fiche générée depuis la file d'attente des candidats (vague 1 du plan de couverture anthroponymique). Seul le champ origine a été recherché (2026-10-06), dans les volumes UNESCO de l'Histoire générale de l'Afrique : chaque piste est attribuée et citée à la page, aucune n'est retenue comme la bonne. Ne pas étendre les autres champs sans appliquer le protocole docs/runbooks/anthroponym-fiche-research.md.

historicalSyntheses.claim: The Diomandé are said to be brothers of the Camara. In the sixteenth century, a group of Malinké of the Camara clan came from the upper Niger and settled in Liberia and western Côte d'Ivoire; at the same time, the Diomandé advanced eastward, settled at Touba and drove out the Dan-Toura, who then occupied the Man region.

The Konyan country, around Touba, is settled by Maninka clans under the hegemony of the Kamara and Dyomande clans. Their legendary ancestor, Feren-Kaman, is said to have driven back or assimilated the Kpelle already there. The author of the chapter holds that the settlement of the Konyan and the Mau, at Touba, must go back to at least the end of the fifteenth century for the Mane invasion to be intelligible.

In a passage on the movements of the Jula groups, the chapter notes, without calling them Jula, that the Diomandé were settling in the centre-west of Côte d'Ivoire, while the Wattara were making Boron and Mankono into trading crossroads.

sources.title: Relevé de couverture anthroponymique EthniAfrica
sources.notes: This name appears on our list of names to document: it was selected as a name to be documented, but no dedicated source has yet been consulted. The fiche therefore exists to flag the name, not for what it asserts about it. Future verification will draw on electoral registers, national statistical institutes and onomastic studies of the country concerned.

sources.title: Histoire générale de l'Afrique, IV : L'Afrique du XIIe au XVIe siècle — chapitre 12, Les peuples côtiers, premiers contacts avec les Portugais, de la Casamance aux lagunes ivoiriennes
sources.notes: UNESCO, 1985; chapter by Yves Person. Printed page 345: the Konyan settled by Maninka clans under the hegemony of the Kamara and Dyomande clans, whose legendary ancestor is Feren-Kaman, who drove back or assimilated the Kpelle; the settlement of the Konyan and the Mau, at Touba, must go back to at least the end of the fifteenth century. The chapter gives no meaning for the name.

gaps.reason: No meaning of the name Diomandé is established in the sources we have consulted: they say where the clan settled and which other clan it is related to, not what the word means. The dates and accounts above are those of their authors; none is held to be the correct one. The Mahouka people have their own account of the arrival of the Diomandé, in their fiche; it is not repeated here.
